brief: Rain arrives over half a day and leaves in a single frame. When rainLeft hits zero the code sets raining = false and does raindrops.length = 0, dropping all ~110 drops between two frames, while the wet sheen behind it eases out over 18 s and the cloud cover eases over half a day. The arrival is ramped and the departure is a cut, and it is the town's largest remaining pop. This is not theoretical: it is the POP at frame 7 that cost iteration 9 a whole diagnosis, and it will keep firing on filmstrips run by iterations that did not cause it. Let the shower thin out instead — the drop count should fall away over a couple of seconds, so the last few drops are still falling as the light comes back.
successLooksLike: A filmstrip across a rain-ending window shows no POP where HEAD gives a 10.99 delta against a 0.48 median, and the largest single-frame change through the ending sits inside the noise floor of that same window on HEAD.
avoid: Do not touch the arrival — it is already ramped and correct. Do not change how long the shower lasts; rainLeft owns that, and this brief only changes how it ends. Time-compress: a day is 55 s, so a fade longer than ~2-3 s stops being an ending and becomes drizzle.
